title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). X/S is a smooth relative curve with ω = Ω^1_{X/S}. P^1_{X/S}(ω) is the rank-2 bundle of first-order principal parts of ω. It sits in the extension 0 → ω⊗ω → P^1(ω) → ω → 0. P = P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) is a P^1-bundle with a distinguished section σ coming from the sub-line bundle.

The page opens by remarking that the construction only uses the extension structure of P^1(ω). More generally it works whenever one has an extension of an invertible Ω by Ω⊗ω with ω invertible.

As the next page makes explicit, a section σ' of P disjoint from σ is a splitting of P^1(ω), i.e. a connection on ω, i.e. a first-order differential operator D: ω → ω^2. A section meeting σ is a connection on ω with polar singularities. The question carried over from the previous page is: for which sections σ' does there exist a projective connection on P (unique if it exists) making σ' horizontal?

Local analysis. Choose a uniformizer t and trivialize the target line bundle L ≅ O_X using t. Write the operator as D(f dt) = a df/dt + b f, with a and b never vanishing simultaneously. Its principal invariant is the meromorphic connection form λ_t = b/a. This depends on the choice of t through the affine cocycle law. The poles of λ_t are the zeros of a, which are not zeros of b. These are exactly the points where σ' meets σ.

The condition at such a point is:
(a) λ_t has only simple poles;
(b) λ_t = 2/t + (no constant term) + terms of order ≥ 1. That is, the residue is 2 and the next Laurent coefficient vanishes.

Check via the Schwarzian. A connection on K = ω with form μ dt induces the quadratic differential −(μ' + μ²/2) dt², which transforms like a projective connection. For this to be regular where μ = r/t + c + … one needs r²/2 − r = 0, so r = 2, and rc = 0, so c = 0.

This agrees with the previous page's condition 'λ² + dλ/dt has no pole where λ does', provided that page's λ is half of this one. With that normalization, residue 1 corresponds to residue 2 here.

Geometric meaning. The local horizontal section of ω is g dt with g = t^{-2}(1 − ct + …). Condition (b) says this differential has zero residue. So it equals dw with w a single-valued meromorphic function with a simple pole: the affine coordinate 1/(z − z0) of the projective structure.

Thus the admissible singular connections on ω are exactly the affine structures obtained from a projective structure by removing the points where the horizontal section σ' meets σ. Equivalently, a horizontal section of the oper P^1-bundle corresponds to a point of the model P^1. Note that P(P^1(K)) ≅ P(J^1(K^{-1/2})), the PGL2-oper bundle.
errors: No mathematical error. The normalization differs from the previous page, where the residue condition reads as residue 1 for λ² + λ', i.e. λ there = μ/2 here. Both are consistent.
The operator should read D(f dt) = a df/dt + b f (b multiplies f). The transcription's '+ b' omits f, though this is harmless locally.

ideas.what: Sections of P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) disjoint from σ = connections on ω = splittings of the principal-parts extension; sections meeting σ = meromorphic connections on ω
ideas.modern_name: Atiyah extension / jet bundle splittings; P^1-bundle of a PGL2-oper
ideas.where_published: Related ideas on principal parts in EGA IV §16; the projective connections themselves are unsure

ideas.what: Local criterion for a meromorphic connection on K to be induced by a projective connection with σ' horizontal: simple poles, residue 2, vanishing constant term
ideas.modern_name: Meromorphic affine connections compatible with a projective structure (apparent singularities, residue −2/+2 depending on convention)

ideas.what: Remark that the construction works for any extension of an invertible Ω by Ω⊗ω
ideas.modern_name: Generalized opers / P^1-bundles with a section of maximal non-flatness

missed.claim: Grothendieck works out, in relative algebraic form over a base S, the correspondence between projective connections on a curve and meromorphic connections on ω with residue 2 and vanishing next coefficient, framed via the P^1-bundle of principal parts (essentially the PGL2-oper bundle). This is classical in substance but is an early scheme-theoretic, relative treatment.
missed.quote: λ_t = 2/t (+ pas de termes constants) + termes d'ordre ≥1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it shows Grothendieck around 1972 handling the oper picture of projective structures in families, possibly with arithmetic characteristic in mind (Cartier operator context of the folder). Mathematically the result is known.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct local computation of the residue condition for singular affine connections arising from projective structures, in an oper-like framework. Classical content, interesting mainly as an early relative and algebraic formulation by Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: '$\mathbb{P}^1_{X/S}\Omega$' should be $P^1_{X/S}(\Omega)$ (sheaf of principal parts), not projective space.
'D(f dt) = a df/dt + b' should be read as a df/dt + b f.
'loi[?] dont l'invariant' is more likely just 'dont l'invariant principal'.
'en un pt de λ irr.[?] zéro de a' is likely 'en un pôle de λ i.e. zéro de a'.
'L non choisi[?] avec t' under the brace is likely 'trivialisé/choisi avec t', i.e. the trivialization depends on the uniformizer t.
In b), the crossed-out symbol before 'dt' is probably a false start; read as 'λ_t a comme développement formel en t'.
